piatz.title: The Complete Guide to Making Mead
piatz.author: Steve Piatz

honeys.name: Orange blossom
honeys.note: Distinctive citrus aroma and flavor that stands up well in mead. Piatz's default for a first mead.

honeys.name: Clover
honeys.note: Widely available, delicate; easily overpowered by strong ingredients.

honeys.name: White clover
honeys.note: Schramm's base honey for several melomels.

honeys.name: Wildflower
honeys.note: Varies widely by region and season. Piatz advises against it for a first straight mead.

honeys.name: Tupelo
honeys.note: Complex: herbs, wood, marshmallow. High fructose; seems sweet even when dry.

honeys.name: Buckwheat
honeys.note: Dark, bold, like buckwheat flour.

honeys.name: Mesquite
honeys.note: Robust, earthy (not smoky); great with hot peppers and many fruits.

honeys.name: Alfalfa
honeys.note: Very light and delicate; can leave a slight waxy character.

honeys.name: Basswood (linden)
honeys.note: Pale, distinct lingering flavor some find harsh.

honeys.name: Raspberry blossom
honeys.note: Golden, floral, light citrus background.

honeys.name: Blackberry blossom
honeys.note: Floral, herbal; no overt blackberry character.

honeys.name: Blueberry blossom
honeys.note: Amber, floral, leafy, hints of citrus.

honeys.name: Apple blossom
honeys.note: Delicate floral.

honeys.name: Cotton blossom
honeys.note: Golden, mildly woody.

honeys.name: Mint blossom
honeys.note: Light sweet mint note.

honeys.name: Star thistle
honeys.note: Used in Schramm's cherry melomel.

honeys.name: Saw palmetto
honeys.note: Used in Piatz's chokeberry blend.

honeys.name: Fireweed
honeys.note: Delicate; typically takes years to mellow.

honeys.name: Heather
honeys.note: Can be lovely but usually needs years of aging.

honeys.name: Sunflower
honeys.note: Indistinct but not unpleasant.

honeys.name: Pumpkin blossom
honeys.note: Earthy to the point of unpleasant.

juices.name: Apple juice / cider
juices.note: SG varies by apple variety (Piatz). Measure yours.

juices.name: Pear juice
juices.note: Piatz: can replace most or all apple juice in a cyser.

juices.name: Wine grape juice (fresh)
juices.note: Piatz: fresh wine grape juice typically 1.090–1.100.

juices.name: Pomegranate juice
juices.note: Piatz measured 1.072 (the USDA sugar figure implies ~1.05).

juices.name: Tart cherry juice
juices.note: No figure in the books — measure it.

juices.name: Chokeberry juice
juices.note: No figure in the books — measure it.

juices.name: Raspberry concentrate (8:1)
juices.note: Piatz: 1 qt of 8:1 concentrate = 2 gal juice. Single-strength SG estimated from USDA raspberry sugar.

juices.name: Riesling grape concentrate
juices.note: Enter the reconstituted SG and dilution ratio from the label.

sugars.name: Cane sugar (sucrose)
sugars.src: Piatz ch.9 (sugar = 46 points per lb per gal)

sugars.name: Malt extract
sugars.src: Schramm ch.11: 1 lb raises 5 gal about 8 points

sugars.name: Agave nectar
sugars.src: Derived from Piatz's Mesquite–Agave recipe (behaves like honey)
